\newdimen\Poster@limit
\newcommand{\PosterCheckFit}[1]{%
  \global\Poster@bottom=\TP@blocktop
  \global\advance\Poster@bottom by \TP@blockverticalspace
  \global\Poster@limit=-0.5\textheight
  \global\advance\Poster@limit by \TP@innermargin
  \ifdim\Poster@bottom<\Poster@limit
    \global\advance\Poster@limit by -\Poster@bottom
    \PackageWarningNoLine{poster}{OVERFLOW (#1): content runs \the\Poster@limit\space below the bottom margin}%
  \else
    \global\advance\Poster@bottom by -\Poster@limit
    \typeout{POSTER-FIT (#1): \the\Poster@bottom\space spare above the bottom margin}%
  \fi}

\begin{columns}
% ============================ LEFT COLUMN ============================
\column{0.5}

\block{Why target selection matters in OCT}{
  \raggedright
  \begin{plist}
    \item In retinal OCT the layered retina fills only a band of each B-scan;
      much of the rest is near-uniform background.
    \item I-JEPA learns by predicting the \emph{latent features} of hidden
      target blocks from visible context, but places targets uniformly.
  \end{plist}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \KeyBox{\textbf{Question.} Does steering I-JEPA targets toward retinal tissue
    give a better frozen encoder for glaucoma detection, with the same
    architecture and latent loss?}
}

\block{Same I-JEPA, different targets}{
  \centering
  \PosterFigure{1}{216mm}{fig_oct_jepa_comparison_final_cr.pdf}\par
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \raggedright
  Only the sampler of context $C$ and targets $T$ changes:
  $(C,T)\sim\Pi_s(\,\cdot\mid A_s(x))$ with the guide $A_s(x)$ of strategy
  $s$. Encoder, EMA teacher, predictor and Smooth-L1 loss are shared.
}

\block{Five target-selection strategies}{
  \centering
  \PosterFigure{0.88}{236mm}{fig_oct_all_strategies.pdf}\par
  \vspace{0.4em}
  {\normalsize
  \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
  \begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}l>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
    \toprule
    strategy & guide $A_s(x)$ $\rightarrow$ target rule \\
    \midrule
    \Arm{random}     & none $\rightarrow$ uniform rectangles (stock I-JEPA) \\
    \Arm{envelope}   & hard MIRAGE retina envelope $\rightarrow$ rectangles sampled on it \\
    \ArmBest{}       & intensity-centroid band, no segmenter $\rightarrow$ rectangles weighted by overlap \\
    \Arm{anatomy-v2} & soft MIRAGE retinal scores $\rightarrow$ tissue-shaped components \\
    \Arm{cover}      & soft MIRAGE retinal scores $\rightarrow$ greedy coverage rectangles \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabularx}\par}
}

% ============================ RIGHT COLUMN ============================
\column{0.5}

\block{Original runs: tissue-directed rectangles help}{
  \raggedright
  {\normalsize FairVision glaucoma OCT; frozen EMA encoder, mean-pooled
  features, linear probe; test $N=\Ntest$ volumes (\Npos{} glaucoma).
  All continuations start from one epoch-25 uniform I-JEPA checkpoint.\par}
  \vspace{0.4em}
  {\centering\normalsize
  \renewcommand{\mathbf}[1]{#1}%
  \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
  \setlength{\tabcolsep}{0.42em}
  \begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccc@{}}
    \toprule
    & \multicolumn{2}{c}{epoch 50} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{epoch 75} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{epoch 100} \\
    \cmidrule(lr){2-3}\cmidrule(lr){4-5}\cmidrule(lr){6-7}
    strategy & AUC & $\Delta$ & AUC & $\Delta$ & AUC & $\Delta$ \\
    \midrule
    \Arm{random}   & \AUCRandomEpFifty & --- & \AUCRandomEpSeventyFive & --- & \AUCRandomEpHundred & --- \\
    \Arm{envelope} & \AUCEnvelopeEpFifty & $\DEnvelopeRandomEpFifty$ & \AUCEnvelopeEpSeventyFive & $\DEnvelopeRandomEpSeventyFive$ & \AUCEnvelopeEpHundred & $\DEnvelopeRandomEpHundred$ \\
    \ArmBest{}     & \AUCOracleEpFifty & $\DOracleRandomEpFifty$ & \AUCOracleEpSeventyFive & $\DOracleRandomEpSeventyFive$ & \textbf{\AUCOracleEpHundred} & $\DOracleRandomEpHundred$ \\
    \midrule
    \Arm{anatomy-v2} & \TAUCAnatomyTwoEpFifty & \TAnatomyTwoRandomEpFifty & \TAUCAnatomyTwoEpSeventyFive & \TAnatomyTwoRandomEpSeventyFive & \TAUCAnatomyTwoEpHundred & \TAnatomyTwoRandomEpHundred \\
    \Arm{cover}      & \TAUCCoverEpFifty & \TCoverRandomEpFifty & \TAUCCoverEpSeventyFive & \TCoverRandomEpSeventyFive & \TAUCCoverEpHundred & \TCoverRandomEpHundred \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}\par}
  \vspace{0.2em}
  {\normalsize $\Delta$: AUC minus \Arm{random} at the same epoch. Upper rows
  fp16 probes; lower rows fp32 probes against an fp32 \Arm{random}.
  \Arm{anatomy-v2} stopped at epoch 75. One pretraining continuation per
  strategy: intervals reflect test-case sampling (\Nboot{} paired bootstrap
  resamples), not retraining.\par}
  \vspace{0.4em}
  \KeyBox{%
    \textbf{\ArmBest{}, no segmenter:} $\DOracleRandomEpHundred$ AUC at
    epoch 100 (95\% CI $\DOracleRandomEpHundredCI$).\par
    \textbf{\Arm{envelope}:} $\DEnvelopeRandomEpFifty$ at epoch 50
    (95\% CI $\DEnvelopeRandomEpFiftyCI$).\par
    \textbf{More anatomy did not add gains:} \Arm{anatomy-v2} minus
    \Arm{envelope} $\DAnatomyTwoEnvelopeEpFifty$ at epoch 50
    (95\% CI $\DAnatomyTwoEnvelopeEpFiftyCI$); \Arm{cover} $\DCoverPeakToHundred$
    from its epoch-\CoverPeakEpoch{} peak to epoch 100.}
}

\block{Which masks actually reach the model?}{
  \raggedright
  {\normalsize Sampler replay in each trained configuration:
  \CRAuditViews{} training views, batch \CRAuditBatch, \CRAuditSeedCount{}
  sampler seeds. Tissue is a MIRAGE-derived proxy, not ground truth.\par}
  \vspace{0.4em}
  {\centering\normalsize
  \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
  \setlength{\tabcolsep}{0.38em}
  \begin{tabular}{@{}lcccccc@{}}
    \toprule
    & tissue & target & unique & loss & context & AUC \\
    strategy & hidden & purity & targets & slots & (\% grid) & ep.\ 50 \\
    \midrule
    \Arm{random}     & \CRHidRandom\%     & \CRPurRandom\%     & \CRUniqRandom     & \CRSlotsRandom     & $\CRCtxRandom\pm\CRCtxSDRandom$         & \AUCRandomEpFifty \\
    \ArmBest{}       & \CRHidCentroid\%   & \CRPurCentroid\%   & \CRUniqCentroid   & \CRSlotsCentroid   & $\CRCtxCentroid\pm\CRCtxSDCentroid$     & \AUCOracleEpFifty \\
    \Arm{envelope}   & \CRHidEnvelope\%   & \CRPurEnvelope\%   & \CRUniqEnvelope   & \CRSlotsEnvelope   & $\CRCtxEnvelope\pm\CRCtxSDEnvelope$     & \AUCEnvelopeEpFifty \\
    \Arm{cover}      & \CRHidCover\%      & \CRPurCover\%      & \CRUniqCover      & \CRSlotsCover      & $\CRCtxCover\pm\CRCtxSDCover$           & \AUCCoverEpFifty \\
    \Arm{anatomy-v2} & \CRHidAnatomyTwo\% & \CRPurAnatomyTwo\% & \CRUniqAnatomyTwo & \CRSlotsAnatomyTwo & $\CRCtxAnatomyTwo\pm\CRCtxSDAnatomyTwo$ & \AUCAnatomyTwoEpFifty \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}\par}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \begin{plist}
    \item Guided rectangles also leave more context visible than
      \Arm{random}: \ArmBest{} $+\CRCtxGapCentroid$ points (95\% CI
      \CRCtxGapCentroidCI), \Arm{envelope} $+\CRCtxGapEnvelope$
      (\CRCtxGapEnvelopeCI).
    \item \Arm{anatomy-v2} has the purest targets (\CRPurAnatomyTwo\%) but
      \CRSlotsAnatomyTwo{} loss slots versus \CRSlotsRandom.
  \end{plist}
  \vspace{0.2em}
  \KeyBox{Target location, target size and visible context are coupled.}
}

\block{How reliable are the guides?}{
  \raggedright
  \begin{minipage}[c]{0.40\linewidth}
    \centering
    \begin{tikzpicture}
      \begin{axis}[
        xbar, bar width=9mm, width=0.52\linewidth, height=62mm,
        scale only axis,
        xmin=0, enlarge x limits={upper, value=0.5},
        symbolic y coords={Normal,Glaucoma,High signal,Low signal},
        ytick={Normal,Glaucoma,High signal,Low signal},
        y dir=reverse, enlarge y limits=0.15,
        axis x line*=bottom, axis y line*=left, xtick=\empty,
        tick label style={font=\normalsize}, label style={font=\normalsize},
        nodes near coords={\pgfmathprintnumber[fixed,precision=1]{\pgfplotspointmeta}\%},
        nodes near coords align={horizontal},
        every node near coord/.append style={font=\normalsize, black},
        xlabel={gross disagreement},
      ]
        \addplot[bar shift=0pt, draw=OIBlue, fill=OIBlue]
          coordinates {(\CRFOneNormal,Normal) (\CRFOneGlaucoma,Glaucoma)};
        \addplot[bar shift=0pt, draw=OIOrange, fill=OIOrange]
          coordinates {(\CRFOneHighSNR,High signal) (\CRFOneLowSNR,Low signal)};
      \end{axis}
    \end{tikzpicture}
  \end{minipage}\hfill
  \begin{minipage}[c]{0.58\linewidth}
    \raggedright
    \textbf{\ArmBest{} band vs MIRAGE envelope:} gross disagreement in
    \CRFOne\% of B-scans (95\% CI \CRFOneCI; all training volumes
    \CRFOneCensus\%).\par\vspace{0.3em}
    \textbf{Envelope plausibility flags:} \CREnvAnyFlag\% (\CREnvAnyFlagCI).\par\vspace{0.3em}
    \textbf{MIRAGE guide:} GOALS foreground Dice \CRMirageDice{}, in-domain only.
  \end{minipage}\par
  \vspace{0.3em}
  {\normalsize Agreement between two automatic guides, not anatomical
  accuracy (FairVision has no layer labels). Bars: unweighted rates in a
  stratified sample of \CRGuideVolumes{} volumes (\CRGuideBscans{} B-scans);
  high/low signal: top/bottom tertile of a signal-to-noise proxy.\par}
}

\block{Takeaways}{
  \raggedright
  \begin{plist}
    \item Tissue-directed targets improved frozen glaucoma probes in the
      original runs, even with a segmentation-free intensity centroid.
    \item More anatomical specificity (tissue shapes, coverage) added no
      further gain.
    \item Target placement, target size and visible context move together;
      matched-budget comparisons come next.
  \end{plist}
}

\end{columns}
